subject: Request: Early termination & cessation-shield language for Acme Health pilot
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Bcc: 
Date: 2026-12-16T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Request: Early termination & cessation-shield language for Acme Health pilot

Vivek / Marissa —

Acme Health pushed back on the pilot MSA redlines this morning. Key ask: a hard opt-out for the pilot that allows them to cease the commitment mid-pilot with minimal financial exposure. They framed it as a "cessation" clause — they want an ability to downgrade or fully terminate during month 1 without significant ramp charges.

Context: Acme is a strategic prospect (EMR integration + potential Dedicated deployment). They requested a 30-day unilateral opt-out with a pro-rated refund minus a small admin fee. Procurement argues this is standard for pilots in their org due to procurement cycles. Legal attached redlines (see Acme_MSA_redlines_20261215.pdf) and a proposed mutual action plan (Acme-Pilot-MAP-Dec15.xlsx).

As discussed with the AE, our preferred outcome is to accept an opt-out but protect Redwood economics: propose a defined ramp-schedule with an early-termination liquidation amount (not a full refund) and language that preserves caching/compute credits already consumed. Specifically the AE suggests: 30-45 day opt-out window, a fixed ramp liquidation equal to 50% of committed ramp value if they terminate early, and retention of any consumed token/compute charges.

As this deviates from standard MSA (we normally have a staggered ramp + no refund), I need an exec sign-off on approved guardrails and suggested contract language. Can you review and advise on limits (cap on credits, approval authority) and whether we can offer this as a one-time pilot concession?

Attachments: Acme_MSA_redlines_20261215.pdf, Acme-Pilot-MAP-Dec15.xlsx

Asks:
- Vivek: approval on the concession envelope (max % of committed ramp we can allow as refundable / liquidatable).
- Marissa: if approved, can you draft a short "cessation shield" clause we can insert into the SOW/MSA and confirm operational billing mechanics?

Thanks — this is time sensitive; Acme is asking for written language tomorrow (12/17).

—

Irene —

Thanks for the heads-up. High-level thoughts: we can make a pilot concession but need hard caps and a simple, repeatable rule so this doesn't become a precedent leak. Two questions before I sign off:
1) Financial hit: what is the worst-case credit/refund exposure if we accept a 45-day opt-out with a 50% committed liquidation? Please run numbers on the Acme MAP today (e.g., quarter-of-run-rate), include any one-off onboarding credits.
2) Precedence & approvals: I'm fine with a one-off concession for strategic pilots but we should limit to Director+ approval and record the deal as an "approved concession" in Deal Desk tracker. Any approval should include a hard cap (e.g., no more than 30% of total committed value refundable, absolute cap $50k) unless escalated.

Marissa — please prepare: (a) suggested clause language that closes loopholes (no refunds on consumed tokens, liquidation fee calculation, notice period), (b) operational billing steps (how we invoice and when we apply credit), and (c) a short rationale for legal (to speed review).

Irene — hold off on final yes to Acme until we have Marissa's language + the finance numbers. If this lands inside the proposed cap, I will approve and instruct legal to accept with minor edits.

Vivek
VP, Revenue | Redwood Inference

Irene / Vivek —

Thanks — I reviewed the MAP and ran a quick financial hit based on the numbers in Acme-Pilot-MAP-Dec15.xlsx. Worst-case exposure under the AE's ask (45-day opt-out + 50% liquidation) is ~ $38,400 (includes onboarding waiver + partial ramp credit). That assumes they exercised opt-out at day 30 after minimal usage.

Proposal (deal desk-approved one-off for Acme):
- Opt-out window: first 45 days following SOW execution.
- Liquidation fee: 50% of remaining committed ramp value at notice time, minimum $5,000, maximum $40,000.
- No refund for consumed token/compute usage (we bill consumed usage through termination date).
- If termination occurs, Acme may not reapply for pilot credits for 12 months unless moved to Dedicated (exceptions require Deal Desk review).
- We will require a 14-day written notice.

Suggested clause (insert into SOW / MSA, concise):
"Early Termination; Cessation Shield: Customer may terminate the Pilot SOW without cause within forty-five (45) days of SOW execution upon providing fourteen (14) days' prior written notice. In such event Customer shall pay a Liquidation Fee equal to fifty percent (50%) of the remaining committed ramp value as of the date of termination, subject to a minimum Liquidation Fee of five thousand dollars (US $5,000) and a maximum Liquidation Fee of forty thousand dollars (US $40,000). The parties agree that all charges for usage and services performed through the termination effective date are non-refundable. This concession is granted solely for the Pilot and does not constitute precedent for future agreements; any deviation requires Deal Desk Director approval."

Operational notes:
- Billing: invoice final usage through termination effective date; apply Liquidation Fee as a separate one-time invoice item.
- Credits: do not auto-apply refunds; finance to process any applicable credit only after signed termination and confirmation of consumption figures.
- Legal: this language was drafted to be narrow; suggest legal review but minimal edits only.

I recommend approving within the envelope Vivek proposed (cap $40k). If Vivek confirms, I will prep the clean SOW redline and upload approved_cessation_shield_language_20261218.txt to the contract repo and loop in legal (Michael Torres) + Acme (Sarah Lee) tonight.
